messages.subject: Variable tracking size limit exceeded
parts:
I apologize for my long message.
I'm rewriting to Stan the Bugs models in ARM Ch.17, but it looks like I can't compile any models with a (scaled) inverse-Wishart.
Better: I can't compile any more such models!
About two months ago I wrote a simple model, just a step toward a scaled inverse-Wishart model:

data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=0> J;
  real y[N];
  real x[N];
  int county[N];
  cov_matrix[2] Omega;
}
parameters {
  vector[2] beta[J];
  vector[2] mu_beta;
  real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_y;
  cov_matrix[2] Sigma_beta;
}
model {
  mu_beta ~ normal(0, 100);
  Sigma_beta ~ inv_wishart(2, Omega);
  for (j in 1:J)
    beta[j] ~ multi_normal(mu_beta, Sigma_beta);
  for (i in 1:N)
    y[i] ~ normal(beta[county[i],1] + beta[county[i],2] * x[i], sigma_y);
}
generated quantities {
  real<lower=-1,upper=1>  rho;
  rho <- Sigma_beta[1,2] / sqrt(Sigma_beta[1,1]*Sigma_beta[2,2]);
}

No problem: I compiled and fitted it. I still have the saved compiled model.
Something has been updated on my system (ubuntu 12.04, 64bit, R 3.0.1), so I've removed and reinstalled RStan, but the compilation now fails and I get the following message:

Yes, but is essentially never tested on Linux (although we do a lot of testing with mingw 4.6 on Windows). Since installing a new compiler is typically easy (if you have root permissions) and can coexist with other installed compilers, I would suggest a sudo apt-get install g++-4.8 .

Ben
